sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct was expressed, purified, and used to determine the cryo-EM structure of V1aR; proper folding and membrane insertion are implied by structure determination, but no explicit ligand-binding or signalling assay is reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: L1 reports full-length WT V1aR with an artificial SP + FLAG at the N-terminus. The canonical topology (computed landmarks) places residues 1–50 extracellular with no native signal peptide, so after SP cleavage the FLAG sits before residue 1 (M); insert_after_residue = 0 is the only consistent assignment. TM1 begins at residue 51, leaving 50 residues of clearance. The position is topology-derived because L1 names 'N-terminus' without a residue number, and exactly one extracellular terminus exists for a prepend on this GPCR. Full-length wild-type human V1aR was expressed with an artificial signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag at its N-terminus in an insect-cell/BacMam expression system for cryo-EM structural studies (PMC12905432). The native V1aR has no signal peptide (topology shows extracellular from residue 1); after cleavage of the artificial SP, the FLAG tag occupies the extracellular N-terminus before residue 1 (M). The N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend on this 7-TM receptor.

sources.claim: To obtain the structure of human V1aR, we constructed an expression vector containing full-length wild-type human V1aR with a signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag at its N-terminus.

literature_notes: L2 (PMC12905432) describes a truncated construct (residues 33–418) with an artificial SP + FLAG + Avi tag before residue 33. Because residues 1–32 are deleted rather than tagged, this is not an insertion into the full-length protein and cannot be mapped to a distinct insert_after_residue junction in the canonical sequence; it was therefore not promoted to a separate site. L2 does corroborate that N-terminal tagging of V1aR is tolerated for structural-grade expression, reinforcing confidence in the L1-grounded site. No ledger evidence supports internal loop insertions (ECL1 110–125, ECL2 190–214, ECL3 313–329) or C-terminal extracellular tags for this protein.
